stated: The Conservative Party will work with Active Travel England to make it safer for people to walk or cycle, including safe routes to schools and measures to protect pedestrians, cyclists, and vulnerable road users, ensuring new schemes have local support first.

source.quote: We will work with Active Travel England to make it safer for people to walk or cycle, including projects like ensuring safe walking routes to schools and measures to protect pedestrians, cyclists and other vulnerable road users. Where new schemes are introduced, we will ensure they have local support first.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly addresses physical safety on streets for pedestrians, cyclists and vulnerable road users — road casualty risk is a core dimension of whether streets are safe, and safe routes to schools is an explicit safety intervention.

Safer walking/cycling infrastructure directly reduces road-accident injuries (less acute NHS demand) and, if it increases active-travel uptake, improves population health outcomes, reducing long-term healthcare burden.

Safer active-travel routes are a well-evidenced mechanism for modal shift away from private cars; more walking/cycling trips displace car journeys, reducing transport-sector greenhouse-gas emissions — the UK's largest emissions source.

membership_note: The policy's primary effects land on healthcare (accident prevention + physical-activity health gains) and the environment (modal shift from cars). Road accident safety does not fit O5's crime/justice/national-security indicators. The safe-routes-to-schools element bears on transport safety, not educational attainment (O7). Cost-of-living (O2) and prosperity (O13) benefits from reduced transport spend or improved productivity are too indirect and contingent on behavioural change to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
